brief: S&P fell 202bps to 7176 (+5% ytd), a sixth straight down day and the longest losing streak since 2024, with a sharp intraday swing of about 400bps that unwound without a clear single headline. GS cites Hunterbrook's AMD short report and fears of renewed Iran strikes as contributing factors, not the cause. Asian AI-linked chips sold off harder (Kospi down 6%, Samsung and SK Hynix down 7% each) alongside heavy semis ETF outflows ($7.3bn last week versus a $6.2bn average weekly inflow, including $5.6bn on Monday alone). Positioning context: large-cap mutual funds stayed underweight the Mag 7 by 722bp as of Q3 2026 and kept seeing outflows, while CTAs cut US equity shorts to near $10bn (lowest since April) and, for the first time in weeks, skewed flows toward buying, a potential mechanical tailwind. GS's standing 2027 view is unchanged: prefers equities to credit, targets S&P 8700 (up 17%) as EPS growth decelerates from about 30% to 18%, and still expects gold near $4650 by end 2027 despite near term downside risk.
